column2: What questions should I ask a health worker about my treatment?
column6:
Based on the passages, you should ask a health worker these questions about your treatment [9][10]:

- What are the different ways this problem can be treated?
- What will the treatment do? Are there any dangers?
- Will I be cured? Or will the problem come back?
- How much will the tests and treatment cost?
- When will I get better?
- Why did the problem happen and how can I keep it from happening again?

The passages also recommend planning ahead and writing down your questions before seeking medical care [9].

column2: What are common procedures for reproductive health problems?
column6: Common procedures for reproductive health problems include **emptying the womb** (a D&E or MVA procedure) [10]; **birth by operation (cesarean section/c‑section)** when normal labor is too dangerous; **sterilization**, which cuts and ties the tubes between the ovaries and the womb to prevent pregnancy [10]; and **removal of the womb (hysterectomy)**, performed only if no other solution exists [10].
